findings: The current catalogue BA-WSK and 2026–2027 OER appendix pages 51–55 establish standalone Mathematics at Leiden, Dutch with some English, 60 EC each year. The 180 EC total is 120 compulsory, including an 18 EC supervised project, plus 24 EC restricted mathematics choice and 36 EC open choice. Year one has 54+6 EC, year two 48+12 EC, and year three 18+12+30 EC. Year-one open study allows nonoverlapping Leiden bachelor courses. Year-three open space may be filled with a designated minor, five extra 6 EC mathematics electives, or a permitted alternative, subject to the regulations. It stays open in this example. The project is research, literature research or both, documented in a thesis, with two talks in one of the mathematics bachelor seminars within the same 18 EC. The sample uses ordinary programme choices, with no double-degree variants.

Algebra 2 follows Algebra 1, Discrete Operations Research follows Combinatorics and Optimisation, Algebraic Curves follows Algebra 2, and the Applied and Industrial Mathematics Seminar assumes basic probability, statistics and programming. All four choices are listed for semester one in their respective years; the catalogue specifies annual, rather than per-semester, elective totals. No module is counted twice. Differential Equations precedes the modelling project and the year-one sequence supplies analysis, linear algebra and probability prerequisites. Bachelor Project eligibility is prior completion of Seminar Presentation and Communication and at least 30 EC of year-two or higher mathematics. The year-two plan supplies both before the project starts in the B234 period. Project-specific subject preparation still applies, including Algebra 1 and 2 for an algebra, geometry or number theory project.

Proof and induction are real shared elements in Logic and Discrete Mathematics; Leiden constructs number systems and develops proof across the sequence. Advanced Calculus is a partial multivariable match for Analysis 2. The systems alignment is specific to transforms and linear systems, while the Leiden ODE module includes broader theory. Monte Carlo simulation justifies the econometrics relationship without claiming the full statistical modelling project. Verified computer vision in term two and data science in term three for both plans. Earth Observation is planned in term four after Sustainability Essentials I and gives the Earth route explicit geospatial analysis. The specialised UCR applications preserve substantive mathematics while the Leiden proof depth and supervised research remain separately visible.
